synopsis: Digital cousins are synthetic forestry sites that reproduce real-site statistical structure rather than exact geometry; the glossary presents them as an alternative to relying only on exact digital twins [f3837, f4272, f13107]. The approach sits between exact digital twins and pure procedural generation, requires real-site statistics plus a generator, and was introduced in a January 2025 preprint [f3841, f4269, f3838]. Chapter 5 assigns digital cousins medium per-site effort, medium cost and medium visual realism, while reporting full subsequent editing of terrain and objects and full support for moving people and vehicles [f4270, f4271, f4273, f4274, f4276]. They remain valid from new sensor positions and heights, but represent a distribution rather than a specific site—a distinction planners must retain when choosing validation environments [f4275, f4272]. The chapter cites Boreal3D forestry work from 2025 and 2026 as off-road evidence [f4277].
